repos.name: Cursor pstack
repos.summary: Principle-led, multi-model engineering playbooks with direct runtime proof and a dormant Benny operations pack.
repos.bestFor: Autonomous investigations, competing designs and adversarial reviews.
repos.caveat: Cursor-oriented tooling and model-role conventions; some helpers live in cursor-team-kit. Benny is Cursor-only and not registered as slash skills.

repos.name: Matt Pocock — Skills for Real Engineers
repos.summary: Small composable primitives for interviewing, deep modules, tracer-bullet delivery and human-controlled workflow.
repos.bestFor: Interactive design, seam-focused TDD and graph-shaped implementation.
repos.caveat: Many engineering skills assume initial tracker setup and live checkpoints; misc and in-progress files are inventoried, not implied stable defaults.

repos.name: Addy Osmani — Agent Skills
repos.summary: Portable lifecycle workflows with explicit verification gates, production checklists and anti-rationalization guidance.
repos.bestFor: A broad baseline from intent and specs through launch, security and observability.
repos.caveat: Per-skill installs can omit shared repository references; detailed JavaScript examples still need adaptation to the real stack.

repos.name: Akash — Agent Brain
repos.summary: An Addy-derived agent organization with numbered conventions, phased design documents, Linear workflow and isolated execution.
repos.bestFor: Opinionated multi-service development with traceable ownership, contracts and delivery rules.
repos.caveat: A personal operating model, not an independent rewrite of every upstream skill. Requires conventions and integrations; some audits, traces and performance testing are explicitly deferred.

skills.name: reproduce-and-fix-issues
skills.summary: Reproduce triaged Slack bugs before attempting bounded fixes.
skills.method: Require trusted triage and valid config, stop on human ownership, verify existing fixes first, reproduce the exact UI symptom twice, then prove before/after and open only a bounded draft PR.

evidence.quote: - The exact discriminating symptom must appear twice through real UI interaction.

skills.name: setup-benny
skills.summary: Install the dormant Benny automation pack safely.
skills.method: Merge the pack without overwriting local edits, keep external config and secrets separate, verify adapters, create reviewed automations only on request, and test thread safety.

evidence.quote: Do not create or update an automation until the user explicitly asks. Never put a secret value in plugin files, prompts, or committed configuration.

skills.name: triage-issue-reports
skills.summary: Classify a Slack report with one thread-only verdict.
skills.method: Freeze source coordinates, read the whole thread, trace cause before routing, deduplicate against tracker and prior verdicts, and fail closed on uncertain ticket creation.

evidence.quote: Classify one Slack report and post one useful verdict in its source thread. Create a tracker issue only for a clear, new bug. Do not reproduce or fix it here.

skills.name: architect
skills.summary: Settle caller usage and types before implementation.
skills.method: Ground with how/why, run an arena of signature sketches, synthesize a contract, then implement or scrap the wrong shape. Human agreement is opt-in.

evidence.quote: Sketch types, function signatures, class shapes, and module boundaries with `not implemented` bodies and pseudocode. Synthesize across multiple model perspectives, then fill in code against the chosen sketch.

skills.name: arena
skills.summary: Race multiple solutions and synthesize the strongest artifact.
skills.method: Give identical briefs and isolated outputs, keep the grading rubric from candidates, cross-judge after writes finish, choose a base and graft selected strengths.

evidence.quote: Read every candidate end to end before picking. Score each against the rubric criterion by criterion, not on holistic feel, and compare with the cross-judge. Agreement on the base confirms the pick.
One synthesized artifact, with a short synthesis note alongside naming the base and why

skills.name: automate-me
skills.summary: Turn observed working habits into a personal mode skill.
skills.method: Mine only the active workspace's transcripts, ask what changed, cluster repeated preferences, author through create-skill and unslop, then propose the personal mode.

evidence.quote: This skill orchestrates three others: an inline mining pass (see step 1), Cursor's built-in `create-skill` (authoring), and the **unslop** skill (prose discipline). It sequences them. It doesn't replace them.

skills.name: benchmark-checklist
skills.summary: Check that a measured speedup is real and relevant.
skills.method: Inspect the harness and machine load; identify the limiter, tune both sides, count errors and real work, alternate at least five trials and compare end-to-end impact.

evidence.quote: 5. **Does it reproduce?** Run each side at least 5 times, alternating (A, B, A, B, and so on) so warmup, lazy initialization, caches, and drift favor neither. Report the median and range.

skills.name: blast-radius
skills.summary: Prove the hidden safety assumption behind a small-looking change.
skills.method: Trace beyond callers, identify the one fact safety depends on, then move it from assertion to source proof to executable or live-app reproduction.

evidence.quote: A blast-radius writeup that sounds right is worthless. It reads as convincing whether or not it's true. So don't hand back the writeup. Find the one or two facts the whole thing depends on and prove them by running code.

skills.name: bro
skills.summary: Restate the last message without jargon.
skills.method: Rewrite the previous reply in concise, ordinary human language; no investigation or code changes.

evidence.quote: Restate your last message. Stop using jargon and speak coherently. State it more simply and concisely, like one human talking to another.

skills.name: correct
skills.summary: Make repeated agent mistakes structurally impossible.
skills.method: Mine recurring mistake classes, prefer architecture then types then lint/CI then tests, prove checks on past failures, and pair each remaining rule with its enforcer.

evidence.quote: 1. **Eliminate it with architecture.** Give each piece of state one owner and each task one supported way. Hide internals so the wrong import fails. Replace hand-synced lists with one source of truth.

skills.name: create-verification-skill
skills.summary: Generate a project-local way to drive and prove the real app.
skills.method: Discover launch, drive, observe and isolation from the repo; generate a verify skill and feature map; execute one journey and preserve evidence through cleanup.
dependencies: Appropriate browser, PTY or HTTP driver

evidence.quote: Run its own instructions end to end once: launch, doctor, drive ONE mapped feature (one is enough; the map exists so later runs can cover the rest), capture evidence, clean up.

skills.name: figure-it-out
skills.summary: Design an auditable workflow when no playbook fits.
skills.method: State a falsifiable done predicate, size rigor and risk, sequence independently landable experiments, keep or revert against evidence, and log decisions.

evidence.quote: When the task matches no playbook, design one.

skills.name: how
skills.summary: Explain architecture and runtime flow from source.
skills.method: Use one explainer for narrow questions; for broad systems run two to four read-only explorers followed by a separate synthesizing explainer.

evidence.quote: Decompose the question into 2 to 4 angles, each a distinct slice of the subsystem. Spawn all explorers in a single message, each with `references/explorer-prompt.md` and its angle filled in.

skills.name: in-your-own-words
skills.summary: Confirm the goal by playing it back.
skills.method: Restate the user's goals and the problem in the agent's own words before solving it.

evidence.quote: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve.

skills.name: interrogate
skills.summary: Challenge a diff with independent model perspectives.
skills.method: Pin scope and intent, launch one reviewer per configured model, deduplicate findings, then judge Act On, Consider, Noted and Dismissed without auto-applying fixes.

evidence.quote: Spawn one reviewer per configured model to adversarially review code changes. The adversarial signal comes from model diversity, not assigned personas. The deliverable is a synthesized verdict. Do NOT auto-apply changes.

skills.name: ketchup
skills.summary: Catch the human up on changes since their last message.
skills.method: Remain read-only, verify current PR and job states, summarize outcomes in under 150 words plus useful visuals, and isolate decisions only the human owns.

evidence.quote: Keep this turn read-only. Make visuals only from what you already have: do not change code, start an app or a job, or post anything.

skills.name: maintain-verification-skill
skills.summary: Keep a project's verification map honest.
skills.method: Check the index, parallel-read source per feature, drive every feature in one live session, and edit only the verification directory; report product regressions separately.

evidence.quote: Only edit the verification skill's own directory (its SKILL.md, features/, and any harness scripts it owns).

skills.name: Make Bot UI
skills.summary: Build a UI whose buttons wake a Grok Bot webhook.
skills.method: Create a reviewed routine, request its sender key through a secret card, proxy requests through a local server, and expose it on the existing Tailscale node.

evidence.quote: Build a page the user clicks. A server on this computer POSTs JSON to a webhook routine. The bot wakes with that JSON. Keep the sender key on the server. Do not put the sender key in the browser, in chat, or in this skill.

skills.name: no-comments
skills.summary: Remove comments and fix the code problems they conceal.
skills.method: Run Comment Sicko, audit scope and exceptions, fix accepted root causes, use architect only for necessary shape decisions, and offer enforceable constraint replacements.

evidence.quote: 1. Spawn `Task` with `subagent_type: "comment-sicko"`. Pass the scope. Pick each subagent's reasoning level and fast or standard speed for the job, per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill.

skills.name: poteto-help
skills.summary: Find the right pstack entry point without starting a costly run.
skills.method: Read the actual routed skill, answer only the relevant question, offer one usable prompt and its source link; distinguish help from execution requests.

evidence.quote: Answer the user's question about pstack, hand them a prompt they can send, and link the file the answer came from. For a help question, don't start the work.

skills.name: Poteto Mode
skills.summary: Run rigorous work through a matched engineering playbook.
skills.method: Copy playbook steps into todos, apply named principles, ground nontrivial work, delegate by role and model, and retain direct verification rather than trusting self-reports.

evidence.quote: Open a todolist whose first items are the matched playbook's steps, copied in verbatim, before any task-specific todos. A step you choose not to do stays in the list with a one-line `skip: <reason>`.

skills.name: principle-attack-the-premise
skills.summary: Test the common premise after repeated fixes fail.
skills.method: Write the shared assumption and find a discriminating observation before trying another fix; follow evidence and remove the causal condition.

evidence.quote: - **Test the premise before the next fix.** Find an observation that would come out differently if the premise were false, and make it. Look at how the failures are distributed, not only at how large they are.

skills.name: principle-boundary-discipline
skills.summary: Concentrate validation at system boundaries.
skills.method: Parse external input once, trust typed internal data, and keep domain logic pure behind a thin framework shell.

evidence.quote: Place validation, type narrowing, and error handling at system boundaries. Trust internal code unconditionally. Business logic lives in pure functions. The shell is thin and mechanical.

skills.name: principle-build-the-lever
skills.summary: Produce a rerunnable tool instead of unverifiable hand work.
skills.method: Do one unit manually, encode it as a small script, codemod or delegate skill, prove equivalence and make it safe to rerun.

evidence.quote: - Do the first unit by hand to learn the recipe, then build the tool. Prove it by rerunning it on that unit and diffing against your hand-done version. Make the lever safe to rerun.

skills.name: principle-encode-lessons-in-structure
skills.summary: Turn repeated instructions into durable enforcement.
skills.method: Prefer lint, metadata, runtime checks or scripts; retain prominent prose only when the lesson inherently requires judgment.

evidence.quote: **Corollary:** If the fix is structural, only use the structural fix. The instruction is the symptom.

skills.name: principle-exhaust-the-design-space
skills.summary: Compare alternatives before committing to a novel design.
skills.method: Build two or three competing prototypes and compare side by side, including interactions whose quality depends on feel.

evidence.quote: description: "Apply when facing a novel UI interaction or architectural decision with no precedent in the codebase.

skills.name: principle-experience-first
skills.summary: Prioritize user delight over implementation convenience.
skills.method: Justify each feature, prototype early, polish the core loop and count both consumers and maintainers as users.

evidence.quote: - Ship less, ship better (polished experience with three features beats rough one with ten)

skills.name: principle-explain-the-number
skills.summary: Explain what a measurement actually measured.
skills.method: Name the observed limiter, rule out skipped work, errors, untuned settings and noise, and keep run count and spread with the result.

evidence.quote: - **Keep the evidence with the number.** Put the run count, the spread, and the limiter in the notes or a linked artifact.

skills.name: principle-fix-root-causes
skills.summary: Fix the first wrong decision, not the visible symptom.
skills.method: Reproduce, follow causal why questions, instrument when stuck, distinguish legitimate states from impossible ones, and search for repeated instances.

evidence.quote: When debugging, fix the fault, not the place where it surfaced. The symptom is where a wrong state became visible.

skills.name: principle-foundational-thinking
skills.summary: Choose data shapes and scaffolding before downstream logic.
skills.method: Trace access patterns, isolate concurrent state, remove dead code, then sequence shared types, tests and infrastructure for later work.

evidence.quote: **Data structures first.** Get the data shape right before writing logic. Define core types early, trace every access pattern, and choose structures that match the dominant paths.

skills.name: principle-guard-the-context-window
skills.summary: Keep bulk out of the coordinator's context.
skills.method: Route large payloads to delegates and size phases, file scope and turn budgets so only useful summaries accumulate.

evidence.quote: - **Size phases and cap scope.** Limit files per phase, set turn budgets, account for mechanism costs.

skills.name: principle-laziness-protocol
skills.summary: Solve the problem with the smallest useful change.
skills.method: Consolidate decisions behind one source of truth; prefer deletion over extra layers and boilerplate.

evidence.quote: - **Minimize the diff.** Make the smallest change that solves the problem. Fewer lines beat "elegant" boilerplate.

skills.name: principle-make-operations-idempotent
skills.summary: Make repeated and interrupted operations converge.
skills.method: Read actual state, apply only the difference, make stale artifacts recognizable and test crashes at every stopping point.

evidence.quote: **The idea:** derive each step from the state that exists, not from what the previous run meant to do. Read the current state, compare it to the goal, and apply only the difference.

skills.name: principle-migrate-callers-then-delete-legacy-apis
skills.summary: Replace internal APIs and their callers in one wave.
skills.method: Migrate callers and tests together, then delete the old API rather than keeping compatibility layers; only where external compatibility is not required.

evidence.quote: - No external users depend on backward compatibility

skills.name: principle-minimize-reader-load
skills.summary: Optimize for layers to trace and hidden state to remember.
skills.method: Collapse pass-through abstractions, demand interface compression, shrink mutable scope and test whether a reader can locate ownership quickly.

evidence.quote: - **Shrink state scope:** prefer pure functions (returns over mutations), locals over fields, fields over module state, and module state over globals. Derive instead of sync.

skills.name: principle-model-the-domain
skills.summary: Replace scattered conditions with a fitting data structure.
skills.method: Choose state machines, typed models, registries or domain-owned modules that eliminate invalid states and repeated decisions, without speculative abstraction.

evidence.quote: Encode the real domain in a data structure instead of scattering it across conditionals. A structure that matches the domain makes invalid states unrepresentable and deletes branches. Choosing it at write time is cheap.

skills.name: principle-never-block-on-the-human
skills.summary: Keep reversible execution moving under asynchronous supervision.
skills.method: Make reasonable reversible decisions and report them; preserve human control of product direction and confirmation for irreversible actions.

evidence.quote: - Irreversible actions (force-push, delete production data, send external messages) still require confirmation.

skills.name: principle-outcome-oriented-execution
skills.summary: Optimize a planned rewrite for its verified final architecture.
skills.method: Allow declared, reversible intermediate breakage at explicit phase boundaries instead of throwaway compatibility code; require full final verification.

evidence.quote: - Use this for planned rewrites and migrations with explicit phase boundaries

skills.name: principle-prove-it-works
skills.summary: Check the actual artifact before declaring success.
skills.method: Run or inspect the real output rather than proxies or self-reports; prefer a deterministic rerunnable check and visible evidence.

evidence.quote: Verify every task output by checking the real thing directly.

skills.name: principle-redesign-from-first-principles
skills.summary: Integrate a requirement as a foundational assumption.
skills.method: Read the current design, imagine it built with the new requirement from day one, propagate through all references and deliver incrementally.

evidence.quote: When integrating a change, don't bolt it onto the existing design. Redesign as if the requirement had been a foundational assumption from the start.

skills.name: principle-separate-before-serializing-shared-state
skills.summary: Eliminate shared writes before reaching for locks.
skills.method: Give independent actors owned files, branches or keys; only serialize structurally when a single mutable object is a real invariant.

evidence.quote: 3. **Only when one shared write target is a real invariant, serialize access structurally** (lockfiles, sequential phases, single-writer actor, or atomic compare-and-swap).

skills.name: principle-sequence-verifiable-units
skills.summary: Make each work unit and delivery step independently checkable.
skills.method: Start from clean trunk, verify each change before proceeding, and stack commits in an evidence-bearing order such as failing test then fix.

evidence.quote: Order work as a sequence of small units, each ending in a state you can check, and don't advance until the current one is green.

skills.name: principle-subtract-before-you-add
skills.summary: Remove complexity before building new structure.
skills.method: Delete dead code, redundant validators and empty references; design for observed usage instead of speculative needs.

evidence.quote: When evolving a system, remove complexity first, then build. Default to subtraction.

skills.name: principle-test-behavior-not-implementation
skills.summary: Keep tests that catch broken behavior and survive refactoring.
skills.method: Imagine a behavioral mutation and an internal restructure; use independent expected values and the caller's public interface to distinguish useful assertions.

evidence.quote: Keep a test that catches the first edit and survives the second. Rewrite or delete the rest. To write a test that does both, drive the code through its users' interface with a concrete input.

skills.name: principle-type-system-discipline
skills.summary: Make invalid states and mismatched identifiers unrepresentable.
skills.method: Brand semantic primitives, parse external data at boundaries, exhaust variants and derive types from authoritative schemas.

evidence.quote: Make the compiler reject impossible states, mismatched primitives, and unhandled variants. Prefer defining errors and special cases out of existence over proliferating handlers.

skills.name: recall
skills.summary: Rebuild recent working context before resuming.
skills.method: Scope topic, dates and workspace; mine own transcripts and the shared record in parallel, check live artifacts, and return a capsule plus next action.

evidence.quote: 2. Lock the scope before searching. Pin the window ("recent" is a real range, default the last 7 days), the topic if named, and the workspace (default the active one.

skills.name: reflect
skills.summary: Turn durable session lessons into targeted skill edits.
skills.method: Read only the active transcript, run three perspectives and a synthesizer, divert enforceable lessons to structural backlog, and wait for approval before editing skills.

evidence.quote: Present the synthesizer's full Accepted / Rejected / Backlog output and wait for explicit approval before applying any Accepted edit. The user picks the subset and may redirect routings.

skills.name: setup-pstack
skills.summary: Configure model choices and reasoning budget per role.
skills.method: Discover actually available model slugs, preserve intentional overrides, ask budget, validate selections, and overwrite an idempotent always-applied rule.

evidence.quote: Enumerate the model slugs you can pass to a `Task` subagent in this session. That is the dependable source. If Cursor also exposes a models API or CLI that lists the user's entitled models, prefer it for completeness.

skills.name: sharpen
skills.summary: Approach the actual goal as a top expert would.
skills.method: Check sources, methods, scope and user-owned choices; adjust over- or underspecification silently, retain an outside correctness check, then do the work.

evidence.quote: Before starting, ask how a top expert would approach this task (their raw sources, their real methods, an outside check that the result is right), what the user is really after, and whether the task is over- or underspecified.

skills.name: show-me-your-work
skills.summary: Keep an auditable decision trail for unattended work.
skills.method: Append one single-line TSV row per decision with evidence pointers; audit it against the transcript and request a different-family review before handoff.

evidence.quote: A single TSV file, one row per decision. Cells stay single-line. Evidence is a pointer, not prose.

skills.name: swarm
skills.summary: Fan out coverage or races into one accountable report.
skills.method: Declare done predicate and race selection rule, isolate writes, pin SHAs and measurement method, drain workers, reject incomplete results and report gaps rather than passes.

evidence.quote: Read the terminal results. Drop a result that does not record the SHAs and method its brief names, and respawn that worker once. After a second miss, record a gap. A gap does not count as a pass.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Write a focused regression test when the local test path is cheap.
skills.method: Reproduce, run the smallest failing check before the fix, implement minimally and rerun; explicitly skip expensive or brittle new tests in favor of useful executable evidence.
dependencies: Existing practical test path or app driver

evidence.quote: Do not force a test when it would be impractical.
Prefer no new test over a bad test.

skills.name: teach
skills.summary: Help a person understand a change, not merely read a summary.
skills.method: Run how and why, preserve confidence language, explain at the person's pace and build diagrams one part at a time; no quizzes or code changes.

evidence.quote: Teach sits on top of `how` and `why`. Get your bearings on what the work is and what it touches, then run `how` for how it works and `why` for why it's that way. Those are real skill invocations that do their own digging.

skills.name: technical-writing
skills.summary: Make technical prose readable on the first pass.
skills.method: Choose one Diataxis mode, apply Google developer style, STE instruction sizing and Global English disambiguation, then remove AI tells.
outputs: Edited docs, RFCs or PR prose

evidence.quote: Write so a tired engineer understands on the first read. Apply all four layers.
Diátaxis structure, Google developer style sentences, STE instruction rules, Global English syntax.

skills.name: typescript-best-practices
skills.summary: Apply type-system discipline in TypeScript syntax.
skills.method: Prefer discriminated unions, validated brands, schema-derived types and exhaustive narrowing; reject raw unknown boundary shapes and unchecked casts.

evidence.quote: | Branded types | Brand primitives with `& { readonly __brand: "X" }` so they can't be mixed up. Validate once at the boundary. A brand comes from a verifying type guard (`input is AgentId`), never from `as`.

skills.name: unslop
skills.summary: Remove recognizable AI prose patterns.
skills.method: Scan stable rule IDs for filler, vague sourcing, artificial contrast, jargon and formatting tells; rewrite concretely while preserving meaning and tone.

evidence.quote: Edit text to remove AI patterns. Scan for the patterns below, then rewrite. Preserve meaning and match the intended tone.

skills.name: why
skills.summary: Recover why a design exists from its historical evidence.
skills.method: Anchor in source and git history, discover available MCP categories, investigate each in parallel, and synthesize facts, inferences, unknowns and null results separately.

evidence.quote: The structure is the one in `references/synthesizer-prompt.md`: The Question, The Code in Question, What We Found, What We Can Reasonably Infer, Competing Hypotheses, What We Don't Know, Sources Consulted, Confidence Summary.

skills.name: ask-matt
skills.summary: Choose a composable engineering flow for the situation.
skills.method: Read recommended skills rather than trusting summaries; route idea-to-ship via grilling, optional prototype, spec/tickets and isolated implementation contexts.

evidence.quote: Keep steps 1–3 in **one unbroken context window** (don't compact or clear until after `/to-tickets`) so the grilling, spec, and tickets all build on the same thinking.

skills.name: code-review
skills.summary: Review standards and specification independently.
skills.method: Pin a nonempty merge-base diff, locate standards and originating spec, run two parallel reviewers, and present their findings separately without reranking.

evidence.quote: Present the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).

skills.name: codebase-design
skills.summary: Design deep modules with small, useful interfaces.
skills.method: Use shared vocabulary for module, seam and depth; apply the deletion test, place seams deliberately and test through the interface rather than internal structure.

evidence.quote: Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured.

skills.name: diagnosing-bugs
skills.summary: Build a tight red-capable feedback loop before diagnosis.
skills.method: Redact evidence, prove one executable failing signal, minimize it, rank three to five hypotheses, instrument predictions one at a time, then fix and clean up.

evidence.quote: Stop and say so explicitly. List what you tried.

skills.name: domain-modeling
skills.summary: Sharpen shared domain language during design.
skills.method: Challenge ambiguous terms and contradictions with code, invent boundary cases, update GLOSSARY.md immediately, and offer ADRs only for consequential decisions.
dependencies: Existing glossary map and ADR layout

evidence.quote: When a term is resolved, update `GLOSSARY.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md](./GLOSSARY-FORMAT.md).

skills.name: grill-with-docs
skills.summary: Interview while persisting domain decisions.
skills.method: Compose exactly two primitives: grilling resolves the design tree while domain-modeling captures glossary and ADR decisions.

evidence.quote: Call the Skill tool twice, for "grilling" and "domain-modeling".

skills.name: implement
skills.summary: Implement a spec or ticket with test and review closure.
skills.method: Fetch and name the ticket, invoke TDD at agreed seams, typecheck and run focused tests frequently, run the full suite and code review, then commit.

evidence.quote: Call the Skill tool with "tdd" where possible, at pre-agreed seams.

skills.name: implement-spec
skills.summary: Implement an entire ticket graph on one integration branch.
skills.method: Read blocking edges, run ready-frontier implementers in separate worktrees, exchange context pointers rather than payloads, merge results and review the integration.

evidence.quote: The tickets are not a list of steps. They are a **task graph** with blocking relationships between them. This means there is always a **frontier** of tickets which are ready to be grabbed.

skills.name: improve-codebase-architecture
skills.summary: Survey the codebase for high-value module deepening.
skills.method: Weight recent churn, explore friction using codebase-design vocabulary, present an HTML candidate report, then grill through the user's selected opportunity.

evidence.quote: Write a self-contained HTML file to the OS temp directory so nothing lands in the repo.

skills.name: pr
skills.summary: Write a visual, evidence-bearing pull request body.
skills.method: Use the smallest diagram, diff sketch or tree, include concrete before/after proof, and classify one-way versus two-way merge danger and blast radius.

evidence.quote: Concrete evidence that the change works. Show a before and after.

skills.name: prototype
skills.summary: Answer a design question with throwaway code.
skills.method: Choose a single shareable HTML state-model demo or multiple UI variants on one route; expose state, skip production polish, and preserve the result on a throwaway branch.

evidence.quote: - **"Does this logic / state model feel right?"** → [LOGIC.md](LOGIC.md).

skills.name: research
skills.summary: Delegate cited primary-source research.
skills.method: Run a background agent against official docs, source and specifications; write one cited Markdown note in the repo's existing convention.

evidence.quote: 1. Investigate the question against **primary sources** (official docs, source code, specs, first-party APIs), not a secondary write-up of them. Follow every claim back to the source that owns it.

skills.name: retro
skills.summary: Improve the environment that produced a session's mistakes.
skills.method: Read session sources and current checks, identify navigation, enforcement and tool-cost failures, prefer deterministic guards over prose, and rank suggestions by severity.

evidence.quote: - **Coding standards**: should the **reviewer agent** be given a new rule to enforce? Should an existing rule be removed or clarified?

skills.name: setup-matt-pocock-skills
skills.summary: Configure tracker, triage labels and domain-doc conventions.
skills.method: Explore existing state, ask one configuration section at a time, confirm the draft, then add pointers and repo-local adapter documents.

evidence.quote: This is a prompt-driven skill, not a deterministic script. Explore, present what you found, confirm with the user, then write.

skills.name: tdd
skills.summary: Build behavior tests at pre-agreed public seams.
skills.method: Confirm seams with the user before any test, reject implementation-coupled and tautological assertions, then run one seam/test/minimal implementation per red-green cycle.

evidence.quote: **Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam.
One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.

skills.name: to-spec
skills.summary: Synthesize the conversation into a tracker specification.
skills.method: Do not re-interview; inspect code, propose and confirm high test seams, capture stories and decisions, then publish with ready-for-agent labeling.

evidence.quote: This skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user; just synthesize what you already know.

skills.name: to-tickets
skills.summary: Break a plan into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges.

skills.method: Fetch current docs first, discover CLI resource schemas, use langfuse-cli for data access and load use-case references for instrumentation, datasets, experiments and prompts.

evidence.quote: 1. **Documentation First**: NEVER implement based on memory. Always fetch current docs before writing code (Langfuse updates frequently) See the section below on how to access documentation.

skills.name: linear
skills.summary: Use Linear as the single source of work and workflow state.
skills.method: Create an issue before work with the verbatim request, place it in project/milestone/cycle, record skips and state changes, search before creation and read back every write.

evidence.quote: | M6 | **Linear is the single place.** No markdown TODO lists, notes files, or chat threads for work; bugs live only as `bug` issues; reviewers file findings as `review` issues.

skills.name: lld
skills.summary: Turn reviewed high-level design into implementable service detail.
skills.method: Specify feature-first folders, types, class diagrams, API contracts, schema/rollback, lifecycle state machines and test seams; keep service docs synchronized and obtain user review.

evidence.quote: The LLD is what an engineer implements from without asking questions. It lives in the service `docs/LLD.md` (`templates/LLD.md`), stays in sync with the code, and is reviewed by the user.

skills.name: observability-and-instrumentation
skills.summary: Instrument every task with bounded, low-noise signals.
skills.method: Use O1-O8: boundary/transition/error logs, tested RED plus saturation metrics, PM-defined product metrics and Prometheus/Grafana/Loki; defer traces/runbooks and schedule dashboards/alerts by milestone.

evidence.quote: | O7 | **Runbooks and traces: deferred. Alerts: provisioned at the milestone the plan names,** together with dashboards; not before.
**metric emission itself is always required.**

skills.name: performance-optimization
skills.summary: Optimize only measured user-visible bottlenecks.
skills.method: Establish real and synthetic baselines, profile one bottleneck, apply a targeted fix, keep or revert after remeasurement, log rejected attempts and guard the primary metric. Retains measure/profile/keep-or-revert discipline; the fork keeps worked optimization patterns inline where Addy moves them into a reference file.

evidence.quote: A fix is a hypothesis until you re-measure. This step decides whether it survives.

skills.name: planning-and-task-breakdown
skills.summary: Plan usable milestones, capacity-limited sprints and disjoint tasks.
skills.method: Start from reviewed design, merge one shared foundation before parallel work, assign owned paths/contracts/tests/points, keep Linear as the task index and close sprints with re-estimation evidence.

evidence.quote: For milestone 1, and any later milestone that introduces new shared definitions: folder structure, shared types, API models and contracts, domain model definitions, test scaffolding, basic startup.
One engineer owns it; nothing else in the milestone starts until it is merged.

skills.name: prd-writing
skills.summary: Write a phased, measurable product contract before design.
skills.method: Read the verbatim request and project PRD, define target users and success target, isolate earliest usable MVP, attach acceptance criteria and affected services, then request review.

evidence.quote: 4. **Scope**: cut the MVP phase, the smallest version a user can use, shipped at the earliest. Everything else goes to a later phase, and what is out goes under "Deliberately not" with a reason.

skills.name: security-and-hardening
skills.summary: Threat-model and harden externally exposed behavior.
skills.method: Map trust boundaries and assets with STRIDE, apply always/ask/never tiers, audit supply-chain scripts, protect secrets and enforce authorization, SSRF and destructive-path checks. Body matches Addy byte-for-byte after frontmatter; differences here are metadata, not a distinct method.

evidence.quote: 1. **Map the trust boundaries.** Where does untrusted data cross into your system?

skills.name: shipping-and-launch
skills.summary: Launch with explicit readiness and rollback gates.
skills.method: Run quality/security/performance/accessibility checks, deploy behind flags, advance staged cohorts using thresholds and error budget, then verify production and rollback readiness. Retains the staged rollout method; the fork still includes a concrete Prisma rollback example where Addy requires a verified command or runbook. Validate that command before use.

evidence.quote: Ship with confidence. The goal is not just to deploy — it's to deploy safely, with monitoring in place, a rollback plan ready, and a clear understanding of what success looks like.
Migration [X] has a rollback: `npx prisma migrate rollback`

skills.name: source-driven-development
skills.summary: Ground framework decisions in current official sources.
skills.method: Detect exact versions, fetch the relevant official page, treat fetched content as data, implement documented patterns and cite each framework-specific choice. Body matches Addy byte-for-byte after frontmatter; differences here are metadata, not a distinct method.

evidence.quote: Fetch the specific documentation page for the feature you're implementing. Not the homepage, not the full docs — the relevant page.

skills.name: spec-driven-development
skills.summary: Write and approve a specification before planning code.
skills.method: Optionally split multiple capabilities, specify objective, stack, commands, structure, style, tests and boundaries; save for human review before proceeding. Retains the gated lifecycle and human approval, but lacks Addy's explicit stop-the-turn-after-spec rule. Phased product requirements also have a separate prd-writing skill.

evidence.quote: Spec-driven development has four phases, preceded by a scope check (Phase 0) that activates only when one request bundles several independently testable capabilities.
The human has reviewed and approved the spec

skills.name: test-driven-development
skills.summary: Prove every acceptance criterion through real entry points.
skills.method: Retain red-green-refactor but add T1-T12: per-criterion and milestone E2E scenarios, race tests, metric tests, contract mocks and isolated data; do not weaken assertions; performance testing is explicitly deferred.

evidence.quote: | T2 | **Every acceptance criterion has a test; tests are never weakened or skipped to pass; the running app is exercised, not only its tests.** |
**Performance testing: deferred, and stated on the ticket when it would have applied.**

skills.name: using-agent-skills
skills.summary: Map incoming work to the correct lifecycle discipline.
skills.method: Identify the phase, invoke applicable skills before acting, surface assumptions, manage confusion and scope, and demand evidence at each completion gate. Routes documentation to the split documentation skill and adds warnings against stale state reporting and hidden delegation, retries, model switching or costs.

evidence.quote: **Check for an applicable skill before starting work.** Skills encode processes that prevent common mistakes.

recommendations.context: I do not yet know what I really want.
recommendations.reason: One question at a time with a stated hypothesis and explicit confirmed intent; it stops before turning the interview into implementation.

recommendations.context: I want design discussions to build shared vocabulary.
recommendations.reason: The interview wrapper composes frontier-based grilling with immediate glossary and ADR updates.

recommendations.context: I need to understand a mature system before changing it.
recommendations.reason: Separate runtime explanation from historical motivation, then prove the key safety assumption rather than merely listing callers.

recommendations.context: I want competing designs and a synthesized winner.
recommendations.reason: Arena isolates candidates, cross-judges them against a rubric and grafts the strongest parts instead of returning disconnected proposals.

recommendations.context: I want small test-first steps with human-chosen test boundaries.
recommendations.reason: Seams are agreed before tests; each red-green cycle covers one public behavior, unlike a blanket coverage mandate.

recommendations.context: I need a practical local regression test for a small bug.
recommendations.reason: The bug-focused TDD skill explicitly avoids expensive new harnesses and accepts the closest useful executable proof.

recommendations.context: I need a broad portable production lifecycle.
recommendations.reason: Specifications, small slices, security, quality gates and rollout checklists compose without imposing a single tracker vendor.

recommendations.context: I need autonomous implementation across a dependency graph.
recommendations.reason: Ready-frontier tickets run in separate worktrees and merge onto one integration branch with sparse context pointers.

recommendations.context: I need independent review of reasoning, not only a final PR.
recommendations.reason: A bounded fresh-context claim/artifact/contract loop challenges decisions in flight; cross-model escalation is explicitly authorized.

recommendations.context: I need model-diverse adversarial review without automatic edits.
recommendations.reason: Interrogate synthesizes independent model findings and separates actionable issues from optional or dismissed ones.

recommendations.context: I am standardizing an existing multi-service repository.
recommendations.reason: The adoption flow inventories and judges conventions before changing contracts, boundaries, clients and internals in safe order.
Phased PRDs, separate HLD/LLD contracts, milestone planning and Linear workflow make the organizational handoffs concrete.

recommendations.context: I need proof through the running application.
recommendations.reason: Generate an app-specific launch/drive/cleanup skill, prove a journey, then maintain all mapped features against source and live behavior.

recommendations.context: I need to trust a claimed speedup.
recommendations.reason: The benchmark checklist demands a named limiter, tuned comparisons, error/work counts, alternating trials and end-to-end relevance.

recommendations.context: I need Slack report intake and bounded bug reproduction.
recommendations.reason: Benny separates thread-safe deduplicating triage from twice-reproduced UI proof and optional draft fixes; this requires Cursor Automations setup.

recommendations.context: I want repeated agent mistakes prevented, not more rules.
recommendations.reason: Correct prioritizes architecture, types and deterministic checks and proves them against historical failures.

recommendations.context: I want persistent interactive teaching rather than a one-off explanation.
recommendations.reason: Mission, learning records, HTML lessons and reusable teaching assets carry progress between sessions.

recommendations.context: I need AI tracing, datasets and evaluation operations.
recommendations.reason: Langfuse supplies a docs-first CLI workflow, complementing the broader low-noise operational metrics conventions.

lineage.summary: Addy and Akash share 24 folder names. 0 full SKILL.md files are byte-identical; 10 bodies are identical after removing YAML frontmatter. Akash splits documentation/ADRs and adds organizational, design and tool skills; review, planning, testing, Git and observability have substantive convention changes. Shared names do not imply independent methods.
